text_fidelity_a: LED Reflective Vest Running Gear with Pouch, USB Charging & Ultralight Reflective Safety Vest for Night Running Cycling This is one heavy duty vest. Probably one of the most substantial I’ve seen for an athletic-type vest, and I’ve seen a lot. I run, walk and ride bikes at night, so I’m always attuned to what is truly visible in the dark, and this one definitely fits the bill. With large reflective  center stripes on each side, the one in the front is actually part of the large center-chest pocket, that has an earbud hole made into the vest. Belly and side reflective is large and bright. Two smaller shoulder stripes in the back and four in the front round out the reflective coverage. The velcro (sorry, hook and loop) fasteners on the side are such that should have no trouble fastened. Then comes the LED lighting. It’s crazy bright! Green in color with three on settings: Steady on, fast blink, slow blink and off. The battery back rests in a special velcro-closed pocket in the back of the center front of the vest. There is a push button micro switch in the front of the vest to turn on the light. There is also a master on-off switch on the small battery-switch unit, and the USB micro-b charging port is there as well. There are visible wires coming out of the battery pack, connected to the LED ends, but the pocket seems to be substantial and protective enough that, barring abuse, should hold up pretty well. This is not a lightweight vest, but if you’re getting out in the dark, go safely. This is a great vest to do it.
text_fidelity_b: LED Reflective Vest Running Gear with Pouch, USB Charging & Ultralight Reflective Safety Vest for Night Running Cycling

Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software I have used a few different Omron pedometers in my day and like other consumers, I purchased this one due to the solid reviews. Anything with an overall rating as good as this product should be worth the money. So, with my old pedometer on the fritz, I decided it was time for a new one and purchased this model.

Omron Pocket Pedometer was okay at first. It does measure your total steps, aerobic steps, time, calories burned, and distance. The accuracy seems to be pretty good and I like that I can monitor my progress and check things online with the software. These are all good qualities and they earn the product some respectability.

Where this product loses some points with me is with its cumbersome display; its tendency to go blank; and the lack of any ability to shut it off. With the display, what I don’t like specifically is the annoyance with looking at your statistics from past days. It stores up to a week’s worth of data, which is great, but if you want to view the data from a past day, you have to toggle back and forth between two of the buttons. You can’t just simply go back to the day you want and then view the steps, aerobic steps, time, distance, and calories with one push. You have to push the button to the left a couple of times, then push the button on the right to view one stat, then push the button on the left a couple of times again to view the next stat, etc. Other pedometers are much easier than this.
Another problem is with the tendency of the screen to go blank. This happens to me anytime I drop the pedometer. I have to then get a small screwdriver to remove the back, move the battery around, and screw it back on. The display will them reappear. And, of course, there is the problem with inability to shut the pedometer off. With other pedometers, you can turn it off or it will shut off itself after a certain amount of time has elapsed. It doesn’t work that way here. The display is always on, draining the battery at a fast rate. Sure, you could pop out the battery after each use, but this is too much trouble. Just make sure you have plenty of replacement batteries on hand because you’re going to need them.

So, taken as a whole, this is device is not as good as I expected and I plan to search for a replacement very soon. It’s disappointing for something from Omron. I have had better luck with other pedometers from this company and cannot give this one a recommendation for the reasons cited.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor Tracker Trail Camera - Eyeleaf HD 1080P 12MP Infrared Digital Hunting Camera Trail Wildlife Game Scouting Hunting for Guarding, Recording, Indoor and Outdoor Security Waterproof, Night Vision Before receiving this camera for review I was unfamiliar with hunting cameras. I was interested in trying it to see what creatures come to the bird feeders after dark. I know foxes used to come and I have seen racoons and other small animals so I was anxious to try this and see if it could capture the action after dark for me (which would save me having to get up in the night or stand watch). It works fairly well, though it eats batteries quickly.

This is a fairly large camera, a little bigger than my digital camera but a different shape. The front is colored in camouflage to make it blend in with the surroundings for which it is intended. The whole unit is solid and is sealed nicely to keep out moisture, with a rubber gasket between the halves of the shell.

There is a hinged door on the front of the camera that opens to reveal all of the controls, interfaces and a miniature screen. There are a number of buttons to access the camera’s features through a straightforward menu system. I found no manual in the box so there is little guidance. There is a CD in the box and I suppose the manual may be on there. Regardless, I found the menu system to be straightforward and easy to understand once I got into it.

Options that can be set through the menu system include picture and video resolution, time/date, lat/long, length of video recordings, timer settings and a lot more. There are six pages of settings, all of which are fairly self explanatory.

There are slots for a standard-sized SD card and also for a micro-SD card. Be aware that neither of these are included in the package and you will need to supply one on your own. The size you need will depend on the resolution you set for pictures and video. There is a USB port and video out port as well (with a connector) so the video can be fed to another source for playback.

The camera takes 8 AA batteries. I discovered that the unit complains when using NiMH batteries that are fully charged, citing “low batteries”. The problem goes away with fresh, fully charged alkalines. The different in voltage is enough to make the camera complain. More of a concern, though, is that the camera draws on the batteries quickly and can run them down fast. This is ok if you check on it often (daily). The camera also can accept a 12V barrel plug adapter but this kills portability.

The might images I took with this camera are a little on the dark end but are clear enough to see what’s under my feeders. Unfortunately, the foxes appear to be gone.

This is a neat little camera. It works well and it is waterproof. It has some night vision capabilities and it is adjustible to suit your needs in terms of resolution and card size. It could use some more documentation, though, and it does burn through batteries, but otherwise it is a good camera.

text_fidelity_a:
Bushwhacker Omaha - Bicycle Grocery Pannier Cycling Rack Basket Bike Rear Bag Rear Accessories - Sold as Pair Some background - I purchased an electric Pedego Interceptor bicycle for my better half. Pedego's frame also serves as a bike rack, and does an awesome job of protecting the battery. The challenge is that tubing is so thick, that 99% of all panniers will not work because the pannier hooks won't fit over the frame tubing. So, I bought a Topeak Uni Super Tourist Fat Disc Frame Mounted Bicycle Rack to mount above the existing Pedego rack. There was some custom work involved, but it turned out great! This pannier fits perfectly on to the Topeak rear rack.

I needed a folding pannier that a standard backpack would fit into, to make it easier just to plop a backpack into the bike (instead of having to load the panniers everytime, then take all the stuff out afterwards). I did a lot of research, and there are very few folding-grocery panniers that have the width of the Bushwacker (Dimensions: 14" Length x 9" width x 10.25" height). Of those that are also this jumbo size, I read that most do not hold their shape very well when loaded up.

This Bushwacker is rock solid, having steel-reinforced tubing to hold it in place. It has a nice bungee-hook set-up to keep it secure, and is adjustable to increase tension.

Tips:
1) If you use a backpack in this pannier, use a good carabiner (we used the sturdy, easy-to-open-and close, Black Diamond Oval Caribiner) to help prevent the backpack from flying out when hitting bumps. Simply plop the backpack into the pannier, attach the carabiner to the top loop of the backpack, and then hook it on the cloth handle of the pannier. Another option would be to use a bungee cord through the backpack, and attach the bungee to the frame.

2) To help prevent theft of this nice pannier when the bicycle is parked, I attached a small cable to the handle (OnGuard Akita Seat Leash Cable - 53 cm x 5 mm), and locked the seat leash to another cable (used to lock the bike seat to the frame). Though it's a very thin seat leash cable, which could probably be snipped easily, it does help prevent someone without tools just walking off with it. Next, I used some heavy duty zip ties to attach the plastic clips (bottom / backside of pannier) to the Topeak rack. So, I don't take the pannier on & off the bike - I just leave it in place.

FYI - I only used one of these panniers (keeping the other as a backup). On the other side of the bike, I built a custom, locking, waterproof hardshell pannier out of a Pelican 1430 case. It's awesome, and it's great to store the heavy chain & u-lock, tools, extra tube, pump, lights, and extra batteries. I used the terrific latching mechanism from Arkel (10 inch length), and also used a seat leash and zip ties to secure it in place (I leave this pannier on the bike also). Happy riding!
text_fidelity_b: Bushwhacker Omaha - Bicycle Grocery Pannier Cycling Rack Basket Bike Rear Bag Rear Accessories - Sold as Pair

Etekcity Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Accessories Gear Tent Lights, Lanterns Battery Powered LED for Power Outages, Survival Kits, Operated Lamp, 4 Pack This small lantern is a little less than 5 1/2" tall and about 3 1/2" in diameter. If you need smaller, then you need a flashlight! As for light, it has plenty! I have 2 LED lanterns 10" tall by 5" dia. and they put out half as much light as these smaller ones. My bigger ones are not efficient enough to read by, these are. I need these strictly for outages, which we seem to have a lot of, and I appreciate the area coverage of these. No, it will not make it easy to read a few feet away from them, no lantern does that, but it will make it easy to see and navigate in a 15' x 15' room.
They are adjustable in only one way, and that is how much you open them. (At just high enough to turn them on, they make great guiding lights for a footpath or a cluttered area.) All the bulbs are on no matter how close to closed it is, so there is no power saving advantage to having it lowered. 12 Hours of emergency or evening lighting outside, is a lot of hours! It will more than stand up to all emergency needs except getting lost in a cave! LOL If it only had 3-4 hours of good light, I would not be happy with this, my first thought is always 'how to extend the emergency light time' and 'is it adjustable'. Well, you can't, and its not....Because of that this would not be an economic idea for an extended camping trip. But this is not being touted as a night after night lighting fix, as an emergency light, I don't need to worry about that.
I joined Etekcity's review program, because I have purchased several of their products and haven't found one I didn't appreciate a lot! As such I don't feel bad about getting one of their products at a reduced price or free for reviewing them. I take my time, and look at all the negative reviews and see if any apply to the product i received. So far.... yes it is pretty light, but no it would not blow away in less that 50mph winds. And i don't think you would be outside enjoying an evening in that kind of wind anyway. It has the hard anodized look and feeling of a well coated flashlight. The handles are wide enough to be easy to carry and a bungee cord or rope will attach them to the side of any tree or post, or you can hang them from a limb or tent pole. Heavy enough not to tip over, and good quality plastic instead of glass or cheep plastic that cracks. I don't see anything cheap or flimsy feeling about them at all!
Don't know what else to say about these, except my other two larger ones are going out into storage and I will be getting 2 more of these to store inside for emergencies. I highly recommend them!
PS: If you DO get a lemon, for Pete's sake tell them! They are very quick and easy to talk to. There is a card in the box with a toll free number, their e-mail address and their website on it (etekcity.com).... all for customer support.

text_fidelity_a:
King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.
text_fidelity_b: King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer

It's much easier going up and, if you were in a good location, you really wouldn't need to put in pegs and could freestand.

The one thing about this tent that I didn't like or understand is why they were put a pole under the fly and have you pull the fly up and over the erected tent like that. GSI Outdoors Percolator Coffee Pot I Glacier Stainless Steel Ultra-Rugged for Brewing Coffee Over Stove and Fire | Ideal for Group Camping, 28 Cup Like most of GSI stuff these pots are made really well. I got the six cup and the fit and finish is very good. I am happy with it.

One really needs to take note of the "cup" capacity of these pots. There are several different definitions of what a fluid "cup" is: 8 fluid ounces, 6 fluid ounces, and 5 fluid ounces. *GSI uses the 5 oz measure.* Thus, the three cup pot will make 15 ounces (3x5=15); the six cup will make 30 ounces, and so on. Actually, a little less when you account for water in the grounds and some evaporation/steam.

My standard ceramic coffee cup takes 10 fluid ounces to fill just below the rim. The smallest coffee star bucks sells is 8 ounces and it's not even on the menu (the smallest on the menu is a `tall' at 12 ounces...just three ounces short of the three cup GSI pot).

I point this out because if you're buying a pot to make coffee for three people who will drink a normal sized cup (or cups) of coffee, you need a larger pot than you might think. Unfortunately, Amazon doesn't show the fluid ounces of each pot.

So, just do the math: __ cups x 5 ounces will tell you what the brewing capacity is and then think about how many ounces you really drink, or plan to brew, and you'll get the right sized pot.
text_fidelity_b: GSI Outdoors Percolator Coffee Pot I Glacier Stainless Steel Ultra-Rugged for Brewing Coffee Over Stove and Fire | Ideal for Group Camping, 28 Cup

Slumberjack 1/2 Person Nightfall Lightweight 3 Season Water Resistant Tent for Camping and Hunting Backpacking tents are difficult to rate because there are so many different price points. This is one of the cheaper tents that I would actually want to carry for 5 or more miles to a camping spot. At 5.5 pounds, this is pretty heavy. For about the same price, you can find good quality tents that weigh under 5 pounds. Tents that weigh under 4 pounds are a little more. If you're carrying a tent for long distances, especially for many days in a row, a couple of pounds saved makes a huge difference.

Another issue with this tent is ventilation when you have the rain fly installed. There is no venting system in this tent like you would find in more expensive tents. On warm nights, humidity accumulates inside the tent, which can soak you and your sleeping bag and your gear. Even here in California that is often dry during the day, evening rain showers are common in the mountain areas that campers love.

On the plus side, the size of this tent is pretty good for a tent rated for 2 people. There is a good amount of floor space and the height makes it easy enough for 2 people to move around a little. The door is big enough for easy entry and exit. Setup is pretty easy, but practice at home before you get to camp (since too often I get to camp when the sun is going down and visibility is poor). Aluminum poles are sturdy enough.
text_fidelity_b: Slumberjack 1/2 Person Nightfall Lightweight 3 Season Water Resistant Tent for Camping and Hunting

Hewolf Camping Sleeping Bag Waterproof - Compact Indoor Outdoor Sleeping Bags 4 Season Great for Adults Kids Youth Teen can be Zipped Together (Blue, Single 32-50F/0-10℃(1.8kg)-Right Zip) This bag arrives snugly packed in a compression bag that is small enough to easily pack into or strapped onto a backpack, either internal or external frame. Unpacking the bag from this sack was a bit of a challenge as the compression straps are sewn onto the sack and move just enough to get the bag out.

I was pleased with the way the bag looked, the outer shell is a slick navy and medium blue poly that does seem to be at least water resistant because when I poured a glass of water on it the water did bead up and did not soak into the bag. The interior is a grey, lighter weight and slightly brushed poly that feels much more pleasant than some sleeping bag interiors that i have used - not as slick. The zippers, and there are two, are a heavy nylon and have a grosgrain draft barrier on the inside. The long zipper on the side has metal tabs on both the inside and outside. There is an addition slide at the lower end of this zipper for further adjustments. A separate, similar zipper is across the bottom. The way the bottom is configured it appears as though the bag cannot be fully opened. Additionally there is a quarter inch or so gap between the two zippers at the corner so a very small amount of cold air might infiltrate.

There is a permanently attached hood on this bag. If not needed for warmth it can be quite wide and used as just a place to rest a pillow. In cold weather the hood can be drawn in quite snuggly by use of a drawstring. On the inside of the bag there is a soft sewn in tube to keep drafts from entering around the neck. There is also a clever little pocket on the inside near the neck just perfect for tucking a phone.

As for size - I am a woman, 5'6" and average weight and found the bag quite comfortable. It is tapered but roomier than a true mummy. I don't think this would be a good choice for anyone 6 feet tall or over, or for anyone more than a few pounds overweight.

I had no problem operating the drawstring, zippers, etc. Putting the bag back into the stuff sack was an average amount of trouble for returning a bag into a sack.

There is information printed on the stuff sack but it is in Chinese so I can only guess about what it says. The bit that I take to be a temperature comfort range indicates this as a warm weather bag 40 to 60 degrees Fahrenheit, although 0 Celsius is mentioned (32 Fahrenheit). If sleeping without a shelter and with minimal ground cover the 50 to 60 would be correct, with appropriate ground cover (pad, ground sheet etc) it could go lower, and with a tent down to just above freezing should be fine.

This is an inexpensive bag but surprisingly well made considering the modest price and filled with some features usually reserved for more expensive bags. Besides the ones mentioned there are tabs on the bottom so the bag can easily be hung up to dry or air out. Mountain House Classic Chili Mac with Beef | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food | 3 Servings I have tried a number of mountain house meals, and absolutely adore the fact that they have a 30 year shelf life, really sturdy solid packaging, and that they are so easy to prepare. They are also incredibly delicious! When rehydrated, the quality level tastes like something you would get from a roadside diner, which is to say, really very tasty in kind of a lowbrow way.

I shared this chili mac and beef entrée with my children. We had it with some vegetables from the garden on the side to freshen it up, because there aren't really any vegetables in here. There were ample enough portions of meat and pasta, and enough sauce and flavoring to go around. I was really impressed with how well they managed to bring all of the flavors together, and how well everything rehydrated.

I will advise that you should definitely use the hottest boiling water possible to make this, because I found that when my water is merely simmering when I pour it in, sometimes the center of the meat chunks or bigger pieces do not rehydrate as well as I would hope. However, when done as directed, these really are great.

The portion size was generous enough to feed a 40-year-old woman (myself) and two small children, with a pile of vegetables on the side. If you are not having vegetables on the side, I would not try to share.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Classic Chili Mac with Beef | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food | 3 Servings

text_fidelity_a:
VINTEX Portable Camping Shower, Portable Shower with USB Rechargeable Battery, Outdoor Shower for Hiking, Traveling, Pet Bath I have had camp showers before, but they have always been manual pumps so I never had to figure out the electronics of a pump like this. I want to prevent frustration that I had in running this by giving you detailed instructions on how to work this. It is too nice of a pump to miss out on.

INSTRUCTIONS
There were absolutely no instructions with this. I was frustrated.

MOTOR
Make sure that the little black motor has the suction cup attachment slid onto the bottom rails of the pump. There is a cord attached to the motor that will be plugged INTO THE BATTERY PACK to run it later.

ROCKER SWITCH
Be sure that this switch is in the off position.

POWER BANK
There is an electrical plug that plugs into the round hole of the power bank. It says that it will charge very fast, but I found that it took over an hour to get to the point where I could have 2 bars on the bank.

READY TO USE IT?
I used this in a 5 gallon bucket. I filled it with warm water about 3/4 of the way up.

PICK WHAT SHOWER HEAD
You have a sprayer like the kitchen sprayer on a sink or a nice shower head to choose from.

INSTALL WASHER
There is a silicone ring available for each sprayer head. I highly suggest that you attach any extras to the cord with the twist tie so it won't get lost. You can also try installing the ring into each head and hope they don't fall out.

SCREW ON
Once the washer is installed, screw the hose onto the shower head. Then screw the other end onto the pump. No need for a washer there because it will be under water.

ROCKER SWITCH
Make sure that the rocker switch is in the OFF position. When the power bank is charged the light on the charging plug will turn from red to green. Once it is ready, plug the power bank (make sure that the power button is in the off position) and keep it away from the water so it does not accidentally get wet.

TURN ON
Using the rocker switch, turn on the pump. The water will come out pretty quickly so be ready.

HOW TO CHECK BATTERY
To check the battery status on the power bank, turn the switch to the on position and it will show with blue lights how much power is left.

TIME
There is about 60 minutes of showering to a charge on the power bank, depending on how often it is turned off in between sprays.

PERFORMANCE
This is one of the nicest portable showers I have tried. The water pressure is fantastic and really does perform like a shower. The hose is long enough to use this in a shower tent. The rocker switch is handy so that you can turn it on and off preserving battery for longer usage.

I love that you can use whatever water source you have handy as long as it does not have debris in it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite being very frustrated at first, once I figured out how to use this, I really love it. I hope my instructions can help anyone else not be frustrated so you can just enjoy the shower.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for performance, but honestly the lack of instructions in the box makes me want to take off a star or two. I won't for now.
text_fidelity_b: VINTEX Portable Camping Shower, Portable Shower with USB Rechargeable Battery, Outdoor Shower for Hiking, Traveling, Pet Bath

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 3-Person Tent I wanted some room to be able to spend time in a tent when it rains. While not as roomy as I hoped after setting it up, it ended up being perfect for a solo car camper. A single size air mattress takes up just about 1/2 the tent. Leaving the other half for keeping some items around, room to change clothes, etc.

I say it ended up being "perfect" because much bigger and it would have been hard too setup by one person. The fabric feels just right, not too thick, not too thin. The zippers worked about as expected on a tent. You have to fiddle a bit at times, but they held up well to my yanking and pulling. I like the dual doors and the screen 'windows' on the doors.

It rained one day and as others have said I stayed perfectly dry. Don't think the over hang of the fly is any kind of vestibule. It's just enough to keep rain out of an open door.

Like most tents you subtract one person from the size . . . this is a roomy tent for one, a good fit for two for sleeping. Two single size air mattresses would be a tight fit in this tent to give some idea of the practical size.

I could go on and on but for the money this was a great purchase and I have zero regrets about buying it. I have no feeling like I should have spent more money on a tent, or should upgrade for my next trip, etc.

I'm not going to take a star off for this since it's not the fault of the tent, but it seems like I got a 'used' tent but it was like brand new. The only way I knew it was used was because A) the box was open and B) some of items had dirt (like the kind of dirt you find in dusty campgrounds) on them. But I figured the dust was from my taking it out of the box/bag, even though I knew the pole ends had not touched the ground yet and they were dirty, but I figured it could have happened, and went on with setting it up. But imagine my surprise when unzipping it for the first time there was a pine needle inside the tent. That was the only debris on the inside, no dirt/dust. It's actually a bit of a mystery since the tent in all other ways appeared brand new and packed well, etc.

The order was filled from Amazon and it was the last one in stock when I ordered. I'm not mad because the tent in all ways performed as a brand new tent. I have had so many good experiences with Amazon that this one little thing is no big deal.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 3-Person Tent

text_fidelity_a: Columbia Women's Boundary Bay Jacket First of all I have had a hard time with Columbia jackets. I have a long rain resistant jacket from them in XL and I have a hard time zipping it up over my chest area. I purchased this in an XL thinking it might fit like the other but I was wrong, its so soft and fluffy. I could probably go down to a size L and I might order it just to see what it would fit like. I am 5'3 and in-between a chubby/athletic build with 36DDD. Initially the jacket was puffier and fuller than I thought. There is lots of room in the arms, the arms are a tad longer for me but thats okay.  I purchased the black and I can say that the Grey color photo is probably the best representation of this fluffy full look. I have lots of room in the chest, back and armpit area. I could definitely wear a heavy carhartt style hoodie underneath and feel comfortable.  I am short so this does make me look boxier and shorter but I need something long and warm for those cold and wet high school football game nights in the Pacific Northwest. It frequently rains here and can get really cold and drop to the teens so I needed something warm and water resistant but did not want to wear a ski jacket. This jacket is definitely warm and I have not stood out in the pouring rain in this but it does repel water. I can not describe the cuffs, it is like a soft waterproof material and will be perfect if your sleeves get wet from the rain and the rain will just roll off. I initially wanted an omni heat silver lined jacket but this seems like it would keep me just as warm. The tail detail is a tad weird and I don't think it adds much style value but its a nice touch. The zipper is a double zipper so you can unzip it when sitting but honestly this would defeat the purpose for me because if I am sitting on the bleachers I want my thighs to be covered and warm. I found that even if I sat down I did not need to unzip the bottom half, probably because I purchased the XL, might not be the same if I picked the L. I wear a size 12 in jeans for size comparison. If you were to travel with this jacket it would be on the bulky side, must larger than a down filled jacket. I would recommend using a travel vacuum bag if you want to shrink it down while traveling.

Vice Pro Plus Golf Balls (Package May Vary) Interesting golf ball. Remind me a lot of the old "Snake Eye" golf balls, which I liked a lot.

They do have a click when hit, but feel relatively soft. The Pro Plus click is a slightly different click. Not louder, more a different sound.

Trajectory is typical of other premium golf balls. At least for me there's no difference. The Pro Plus seems slightly lower, but marginally so.

Distance is the same as other premium balls as well. The Pro Plus seems to roll a bit more due to the marginally lower trajectory - 2-3 yards is all.

Spin is noticeable with shorter irons. Drives seem to be lower spin - as advertised.

Are they a ProV1 clone, I would say yes. Thus, I'll buy some more and probably order more than one dozen to get the discounted price from Vice.

I also bought Pro balls and like the Pro Plus a little better, but that's a personal thing. I wouldn't hesitate to use either every round.

Regardless of Pro or Pro Plus, I definitely think you get the same ball for much less.
text_fidelity_b: Vice Pro Plus Golf Balls (Package May Vary)

It also tracks how many flights of stairs I've climbed, as well as tracking individual workouts, number of active minutes daily, and other stats. text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Bocce Ball Set — 8 All Weather Bocce Balls and 1 Pallino — Beach, Backyard Lawn or Outdoor Party Game — Professional, American, and Starter Set Options I like bocce and I was thrilled to have the opportunity to review this set. I was particularly interested in this set because it is marketed as a “professional” set. As a casual bocce set this is great, but as a professional set it’s out of specifications, by more than a little. Since it is priced as a professional set, it misses the mark, though it is fine for casual and family play.

I decided to do a little digging to see what would designate a bocce set as a “professional” set. According to the Bocce Standards Association (yes, seriously), each ball should be a specific size and weight. Of interest is the weight range: 920g +/- 10g (2 lbs.). That’s a tight range of weights, though for sporting equipment used in professional or tournament play that’s not unusual. I measured all 8 balls on a calibrated scale, set to measure in grams. The lightest ball in my set is 947g, and the heaviest is 1026g (2.25 lbs.). Every single ball is outside of the range. I could see being a little outside of the range, but over 100g is way off. Since the spread between the highest and lowest in my set is about 80g, and the specifications allow for a 20g spread between the extremes, this is not a scale problem. Most players wouldn’t even notice, but that’s not the point.

As a casual set, this is a fine bocce set and should last for years. The balls are solid and made of some form of resin, are consistent in appearance and though do get surface scratches during play and transport (very normal), they’re rugged and should not break, crack or chip unless abused or purposely damaged. The set comes in a nylon carry bag and includes a rule book.

This is a nice casual set, not a professional set. The balls are out of spec which makes it unsuitable for true tournament play. And as a casual set, it’s a bit expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Bocce Ball Set — 8 All Weather Bocce Balls and 1 Pallino — Beach, Backyard Lawn or Outdoor Party Game — Professional, American, and Starter Set Options

I didn't really NEED it, but it sure looked like a good idea and a good addition to my hiking/backpacking/fly fishing arsenal. First, let me say I was impressed with the quality. As a full piece of steel with a full tang, it is unlikely to separate at any time. While the handle is small owing to the size of the blade, it is still manageable. The handle has a nice big eyelet to which a safely line could be tied or, should one be in the mood, to use as a starter to tie to a branch to make a spear.

The sheath is also much better than I had expected. I had originally thought the sheath was just going to be straight nylon. This is not the case. There is a hard plastic liner within that secures the knife blade and keeps the blade from cutting up the sheath. Also, what looks like a thumb spot from the handle doubles as a non-mechanical locking mechanism within the sheath. It requires a decent tug to pull the knife out. This would certainly curtail accidental fallouts while walking or sprinting.

The nylon strap is both strong and adjustable. Overall, I'm quite impressed with this little gem.
text_fidelity_b: CRKT Sting Fixed Blade Knife with Sheath: Everyday Carry Boot Knife, Double Edged Powder Coated Stainless Steel, Contoured Handle, Nylon Sheath with Strapping for Carry Options 2020

text_fidelity_a: Oakley DRT 5 Bike-Helmets As a disclaimer, I purchased this helmet as it did seem to check all of the boxes and then made the decision to buy it after finding it at a significant markdown combined with some credits from Amazon.  It was hard to pass up.  Overall I find it to be a good quality helmet.  As others have mentioned in reviews, the feel on the head is somewhat like the way a "hardhat" sits on the head- a little high center, which must have been the design.  Ventilation seems very good.  I went with size L as I am on borderline, between M and L.  But in past MTB helmet purchases,  the M felt too small.  This helmet I think I could have gone with an M and been okay.  In this case, I do wear a "bandana" or "do-rag" under the helmet.  Other reviewers commented about its weight, that it is heavier than most MTB helmets but after wearing it for rides lasting several hours, the weight of the helmet was never an issue or even a thought.  I suffered no headaches from the fit and tension of the helmet as reported by other reviewers.  Pos that stand out; 1.  it feels substantial as far as protection & MIPs, 2.  Simple design as far as headband tension system that worked well for me with the goal to be sunglass friendly.  3. comfortable.  4. Its basic design seems well made and simple (with KISS being the standard).  And so being a good basic design, it feels like it will do for which it was designed, very well.

text_fidelity_a:
Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs I have other Mazama water bladders, and really wanted to like this. I bought it for a trip to the national parks in UT where you should be carrying more water. The good is that its a big reservoir, and the hose is thicker so the rate of flow is higher than their other hoses. What I love about Mazama is the magnetic holder for the hose, and this one is even better because there is some play in it where as the normal version can pop off at times (I generally wear it while mountain biking and its fine, but if there isn't enough slack in the hose it will pop off the magnet).

What I don't like about this one...the closure for the bladder is not secure. I found out by dumping about two liters of water over me when it was in my backpack and I bent forward. I know it looks like it should work, but because its plastic and malleable there is play there and its not perfect. The "lock" wiggles even without pressure, so its suspect to begin with. The way it opens is nice for cleaning, drying, and filling, and the "spine" is helpful for carrying and moving it around. These features cannot make up for the closure however, and I worry about it whenever the bladder is full. I'm also not a fan of the way the bite valve works...it can be left full open and water will just run out, or you can get it to work if you bite a little...but just a little because if you bit too much the rubber tip falls off. Squirely bugger.

When using in the future I might add a clamp or something to ensure the closure can't slip off, and will use my other hose vs this one.
text_fidelity_b: Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs

Extremus Rendu Soft Cooler, 12/20/30 Can Updated Insulated Cooler Bag, Portable and Waterproof Beach Cooler with 100% Leakproof Zipper, Large Capacity for Fishing, Kayaking, Camping, Beaches & Trips We buy our milk from a special farmer that only does grass fed milk. It is not too bad usually, except in the summer, it is tough to keep the milk cold as we go to and from the farm as it is not near our home. This cooler answers that problem.

HOW TO OPEN
This comes with a zipper and an extra pull included. I can see why. This zipper is quite difficult to use. The pack includes a lubrication tube and tells you how to keep the zipper working. Well, I did it several times and it still is not easy to slide the zipper.

INSIDE
The inside is quite a bit smaller than the outside due to the insulation. Our milk bottles will only fit long ways instead of sideways as I thought they would.

DOES IT KEEP THINGS COLD?
I have to say that I got some yogurt the other day and did not have ice to put in the cooler. I put in 3 containers of yogurt which were quart sized. I had them in there for about 5 hours. When I got home, the yogurt was still pretty cold. I am impressed.

STRAPS/HANDLE
The straps and handle on this cooler are really great. The shoulder strap makes it easy for me to carry this along with the other things I have to carry in the house It is comfortable and works out well.

LEAKS?
This did not leak so far when ice melts.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is the perfect cooler for getting our milk this summer. It will allow me to make the trip and not be so concerned about keeping the milk cold in our other coolers because this one with some ice included will work perfectly.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS although the zipper on this is very frustrating and I would like to take off a star, but I don't think it is that bad at this point. I will update of anything changes.
text_fidelity_b: Extremus Rendu Soft Cooler, 12/20/30 Can Updated Insulated Cooler Bag, Portable and Waterproof Beach Cooler with 100% Leakproof Zipper, Large Capacity for Fishing, Kayaking, Camping, Beaches & Trips

text_fidelity_a:
Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete/Fixed Blade Knife with Nylon Sheath I am a knife collector who also buys knives as tools to use while trimming mangroves and removing invasive vegetation from the wetlands on our property in Southwest Florida. Twice a year I find myself in the wetlands trimming away so that we can maintain our water view as per current regulations in place. Because of the hazardous footing, thick vegetation, and dangerous flora and fauna -- I primarily use machetes and hatchets for my work. I want to be able to see and hear any of the frequent obstacles I encounter daily in that dangerous mess.

The average width of the limbs I am currently trimming require a short chopping motion since the trees are so tightly packed together. I usually depend on an Esee Lite Machete for most of the work but it is too long and requires swinging it to be most effective, hence my serch for a good chopper. This Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete fits the bill. It is well built with a full taexng ending in a butt plate. The blade is a full 12" of 440 stainless steel and it has a pommel to help protect your swinging hand.

It arrived sharp enough to shave hair off my arm and to pass the paper test. The cutting side is thin and curved with the top of the blade carrying the weight for more effective chopping. It even has several serrations at the top of the blade for cutting/sawing. The pakkawood handle is fastened to the full tang blade with three bolts and the machete itself has a nice solid feel. The handle is a bit small and slippery for me but that is easily remedied with grip tape and gloves.

Here's the kicker. Some people might collect this type of knife because it is well assembled, visually appealing, and feelsgood in the hand. However I bought this as a working tool for a very reasonable price and feel that it offers considerable value for the cost. Looking for an effective chopper? Search no more. text_fidelity_a:

The most important is that the waist straps are not sewn, and can easily slip out of the buckle. That very thing happened to me while shuffling around Europe. One of the primary reasons I chose this pack over some others is because of the well-sized waist pads and strap. Unlike other packs I have had, the nylon webbing was simply passed through the buckles, but never sewn to itself to prevent slipping through. That little "slip" can make a huge difference in how your body holds up your gear. Luckily, I found a Sport Scheck in Germany that had 2" webbing and replacement buckles. This time I made them a few inches longer so they could be tied off at the ends before I was able to get them sewn on.
Otherwise, the only other design issue I have is with the long strap that goes across the front of the pack. It's always in the way, and when the pack is full it leaves little room to strap anything to it. If it were a little longer and/or could be easily removed, it would be that much better. Fix those two issues and it's a 5* product.

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter Obviously, judging by my profile name, I'm a girl. When it is time for me to start a fire, I need something that works right the first time with my smaller hands and does not break all my short but feminine nails. I have used a number of strikers and fire starters with hilariously varying results. Most are okay-ish. I don't like skinny little strikers that you have to rub with a piece of hacksaw blade which often has a back side that is almost as sharp and jagged as the business end of the blade. I don't like short micro strikers where you end up lighting your hangnails on fire along with the tinder because your hand was so close. (This doesn't actually happen but you get the picture.)

When I first bought this BlastMatch my husband immediately claimed it as his and it disappeared from the face of the earth for over two years. That should have been my first clue that it was the best striker out there. Every once in awhile it would resurface to light the fire pit in the back yard but it would quickly be whisked away to a back pocket and once again vanish from existence as rapidly as it had reappeared. I had no idea where he was hiding it so I simply had to resort to using other strikers I had purchased that worked well enough. They just were not as quick and easy as this one.

Let's talk about what I love. First of all, it has a big, thick firesteel rod that is the thickest I own. (See the picture I uploaded.) This means it will most likely last for the advertised number of strikes. Second, my son has been able to use this to start a fire on our camp outs since he was 7. It's really, really easy. to use. Not really that easy to open but you quickly get the hang of it. Basically you open it, use your thumb to depress the metal scraper on one side and then push down. A bright yellow, orange and white colored shower of sparks will greet you like an angry sparkler gone awry and set alight anything remotely resembling tinder. (A friend who first demonstrated his to us set the fine fibers of our living room rug on fire. After tamping out the little glowing embers, we were sold.)

My husband confiscated the first one I bought and would not so much as let me lay eyes on it so I decided to buy myself a second one. I had given the other crappy fire rods we had somehow picked up along the way to my boy scout son, which was surprisingly safe since they don't hardly light a thing, and proceeded to replace them all with a tool that worked. Since we have one BlastMatch from 2014 and one from 2016, I decided I would compare them side-by-side to see if the product has had any visible changes or become more flimsy as reviewers have insisted. I couldn't find a single difference. The plastic on each was the same thickness, the rod was the same diameter and they both opened with the same springy force.

They give a generous shower of sparks and if you get it anywhere close to a tinder ball, you are going to start a fire with one push. It catches that easily. I am very pleased with BOTH purchases and will continue to use these until they break. (If they do, I'll be right back here to complain.) While we don't use our BlastMatch every single day, we have used the original one somewhere around 50 or more times since my husband is a scout leader and it is still going strong with no cracks in the plastic and no damage visible anywhere to the striker. If you want to be on the safe side, wait until the price drops to twelve or less and then make your purchase. I have seen them as low as ten at various times of the year so your patience can pay off. And do not use your BlastMatch while drunk or trying to impress women. Not that the reviewers who broke theirs were either drunk or able at all to impress women - I'm just giving you some general good advice.

I bought both of my strikers at full price. I do not work for BlastMatch. I don't even particularly like catching things on fire. I just like roasting marshmallows. And Starburst. Happy camping everyone!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter
